device.name: iQOO Z7s

key_finding.title: KleidiAI accelerates only Q4_0 and Q8_0 - not the K-quants
key_finding.evidence: llama.cpp emits: 'kleidiai: no kernel for tensor type q4_K, not accelerated by KleidiAI (kernels available for Q4_0 and Q8_0)'
key_finding.implication: The most widely shipped mobile quantization (Q4_K_M) misses the Arm-optimized kernels entirely. Staying inside {Q4_0, Q8_0} is worth ~3x on time-to-first-token on this SoC.
key_finding.measured: Q8_0 prefill 67.4 t/s and Q4_0 49.2 t/s vs Q4_K_M 29.3 t/s (cool device, isolated runs)

uniform_baselines.note: Isolated runs on a cool device. Perplexity chunk counts differ between sweeps and are labelled per entry; only compare ppl at equal chunks.

summary.generation_cost: -31% sustained tokens/sec (larger model is more bandwidth-bound per token)

frontier_sweep.note: Exhaustive k-sweep over the same axis Anvil searched: protect the k most quant-sensitive layers at Q8_0, leave the rest at Q4_0. Measured at 4 perplexity chunks, same as the search. Feasibility bar = Q4_K_M reference ppl 9.605.
conclusions: Anvil's searched configuration (k=20) is the SMALLEST feasible point on the measured frontier - the search landed on the optimum, not merely near it.

The frontier is non-monotonic (k=16 is worse than k=12; k=24 worse than k=20). Protecting more layers does not reliably improve quality - WHICH layers are protected matters. This is a direct argument for measurement-driven search over any fixed heuristic, though part of the wobble is 4-chunk perplexity noise.

Uniform Q4_0 (k=0, 945 MiB, ppl 10.508) is worse quality than Q4_K_M at essentially the same size (935 MiB, ppl 9.605) - so simply switching to the KleidiAI-fast type is not enough on its own. The per-layer mix is what recovers the quality while keeping the fast kernels.
Mapping this frontier cost 8 on-device evaluations (33.7 min); Anvil reached the same optimum inside its 14-evaluation budget while also measuring off-axis configurations.

live_demo.command: llama-cli -m anvil_best.gguf -t 4 -p "Explain why quantizing a neural network makes it faster, in two sentences." -n 80
live_demo.reported_speed: prompt 33.9 t/s, generation 5.4 t/s (llama-cli, warm device)

caveats: The Snapdragon 695 throttles under sustained load; a benchmark taken immediately after ~2h of continuous quantization read 22.7 t/s prefill for the same config that reads 52.6 t/s on a cooled device. All headline numbers are from cooled, back-to-back runs.
llama-bench generation (tg) numbers carry high variance on this SoC (stddev up to ~1.8 t/s); prefill (pp) is far more stable.
Search used 4 perplexity chunks to fit the evaluation budget; the F16 and Q4_K_M references were measured at the same 4 chunks so the comparison is like-for-like.
Anvil's per-layer sensitivity prior (outer layers matter more) seeds the surrogate; it is calibrated online from measured perplexity.
